parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe the structure of a benzene molecule, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$.

Your answer should include:
- the shape of the molecule
- the relative lengths of the $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bonds
- bond angles
- the hybridisation of the carbon atoms
- the overlap between orbitals that produces each type of bond present.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
Benzene can be used as a starting material to produce phenylamine by a two-step synthesis.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}
parts.text:
(i) Step 1 is the reaction of benzene with $\text{NO}_2^{+}$ ions.

Complete the mechanism and draw the intermediate of step 1.
Include all relevant charges and curly arrows to show the movement of electron pairs.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: (ii) State the name of the mechanism in (b)(i).

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
(iii) Identify the reagents needed to produce $\text{NO}_2^{+}$ ions.

Write an equation to explain how these reagents produce $\text{NO}_2^{+}$ ions.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: (iv) Give reagents and conditions for the production of phenylamine from nitrobenzene in step 2.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: (i) Write an equation for this reaction. You may use structural or displayed formulae.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: (ii) Name the organic product of this reaction.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: (iii) Describe two observations that can be seen when phenylamine reacts with $\text{Br}_2\text{(aq)}$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Describe the relative basicities of ammonia, ethylamine and phenylamine, starting with the least basic.
Explain your answer in terms of their structures.
<  <
least basic most basic

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem: 1,3-diaminopropane, $\text{H}_2\text{NCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$, can be used to make polyamides.
parts.text: (i) Identify one compound that would react with 1,3-diaminopropane to form a polyamide.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
(ii) Draw a section of the polymer chain formed from 1,3-diaminopropane and the compound you chose in (e)(i).

Your answer should:
- include four monomer residues (two of each type of monomer)
- show the amide link fully displayed
- clearly identify one repeat unit of this polymer.
